name: Kimi Räikkönen
milestone_by_age_26: Made Formula One debut with Sauber in 2001 at age 21, achieved maiden podium on debut with McLaren in 2002, won first Grand Prix at Malaysia in 2003 at age 23, and won seven Grands Prix finishing runner-up to Fernando Alonso in the 2005 championship at age 26.

He dominated the 2000 British Formula Renault Championship with Manor, prompting Sauber to sign him for F1 in 2001 despite having only 23 car races to his name. He moved to McLaren in 2002 and won his first Grand Prix in 2003.
family_context_summary: Family was not wealthy; father Matti worked as a taxi driver and nightclub bouncer to fund karting. Funds diverted to racing meant plans to install an indoor bathroom were postponed. Grew up in Espoo, Finland with brother Rami who also became a rally driver. At 16, he left school and enrolled in a mechanics course.
parent_family_domain_summary: Parents were not in motorsport. Father worked multiple jobs (taxi driver, bouncer) to fund karting. No inherited motorsport network or domain expertise.
primary_early_advantage_tags: natural driving talent, karting from age 10, Finnish motorsport tradition, Manor Formula Renault, Sauber F1 debut, financial constraint, Mugello test
evidence_summary: Räikkönen began karting at 10 in Espoo, Finland. His family was not wealthy — his father worked as a taxi driver and nightclub bouncer to fund racing, postponing indoor bathroom installation. Despite financial constraints, his natural talent was extraordinary: he won four karting championships between 1995-1998, dominated the 2000 British Formula Renault with Manor, and impressed Sauber so much at a Mugello test that they signed him for F1 at 21 with only 23 car races to his name. He won his first Grand Prix at 23 and was championship runner-up at 26. His rapid rise from karting to F1 in just 11 years, bypassing conventional development, demonstrates exceptional physical/athletic talent.
